text: After Avdiivka fell in February 2024, Russia drove west for Pokrovsk, the road and rail hub of western Donbas.
Russia broke through at Prohres in July 2024.
Russia took Novohrodivka in the autumn of 2024.
Russia took Selydove in the autumn of 2024.
After frontal attacks stalled at the edge of Pokrovsk, Russia tried through the winter of 2024–25 to turn Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad from the south-west, then from the east.
In January 2025 Russia cut the highways from Pokrovsk to Kostiantynivka and to Mezhova.
Ukrainian counter-attacks near Pokrovsk in February 2025 won back a few villages.
From July 2025 the battle for Pokrovsk became the war's defining drone fight.
From July 2025 Russian FPV teams, Rubikon among them, put every road into Pokrovsk under fire control.
ISW judged that Russian drone fire control over the roads had already denied Ukraine the use of Pokrovsk as a logistics hub by July 2025.
Russian infantry at Pokrovsk no longer stormed positions in 2025 but seeped through in groups of two to three, by the hundred a day.
Russian infiltrators walked for days from Selydove to reach Pokrovsk.
On 11 August 2025 Russian infiltration groups opened a 15 km wedge towards Dobropillia.
The 1st Azov Corps and other reserves cut off the Dobropillia wedge and cleared it by late October 2025.
About 200–250 Russian infiltrators had accumulated inside Pokrovsk by late October 2025.
More than 300 Russian infiltrators were inside Pokrovsk after the November 2025 fog.
By late 2025 the Ukrainian garrison of Pokrovsk was squeezed into the city's northern quarters.
By late 2025 the Ukrainian garrison of Myrnohrad depended on a single drone-watched road.
Russia announced the capture of Pokrovsk on 1 December 2025.
Russia announced the capture of Myrnohrad on 27 December 2025.
Ukraine held parts of both Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad into late January 2026.
Russian infiltrators entered Pokrovsk in mid-July 2025.
The Russian infiltrators who entered Pokrovsk in July 2025 were cleared by 15 August 2025.
Pokrovsk became a grey zone from late October 2025.
Russia claimed the capture of Pokrovsk on 1 December 2025.
On 1 December 2025 a NATO official said Russia held more than 95% of Pokrovsk.
In December 2025 Ukraine still claimed to hold about 13 of Pokrovsk's 29 km².

On 11 August 2025 the Dobropillia wedge was about 15 km deep and 5–6 km wide.

Ukrainian forces retook Kucheriv Yar on 22 October 2025.
Syrskyi claimed that more than 180 km² was liberated in the Dobropillia operation.
The Ukrainian Dobropillia operation was declared complete on 29 November 2025.
Hryshyne, 2 km north-west of Pokrovsk, was still contested in mid-April 2026, and Russia did not break through beyond the towns.

text: Russia did not exploit the fall of Pokrovsk.
Ukrainian soldiers repeatedly said there was no order to leave Pokrovsk or Myrnohrad.
The 68th and 155th brigades left Pokrovsk from late October 2025.
Ukraine abandoned the salient south of Pokrovsk on 8 December 2025.
In February 2026 Ukraine made a short fall-back north of Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad.
"A deliberate regrouping" as a description of the Ukrainian exit from Pokrovsk is the analyst Oleksandr Kovalenko's, not an official statement.
notes: KB correction: an existing claim calls the withdrawal a deliberate regrouping without naming the analyst

text: Russia advanced just under 50 km on the Pokrovsk axis from late February 2024 to early January 2026, about 70 m a day, slower than the Allies on the Somme.
Syrskyi said about 7,000 Russians were killed and 15,000 became casualties in total on the Pokrovsk axis in January 2025.
The Guardian read the same January 2025 briefing as 7,000 Russians killed plus 15,000 wounded or missing on the Pokrovsk axis.
notes: OUTCOME; a variant reading of the Syrskyi figures, which gives 15,000 as total casualties

Zelensky said about 25,000 Russians were confirmed killed on video front-wide in October 2025, "most" of them on the Pokrovsk front.

Avdiivka fell in February 2024, and the Russian drive west towards Pokrovsk began.
On 19–20 July 2024 Prohres fell to Russia in about 48 hours after a large assault.
In July 2024 a front-line brigade's chaotic withdrawal at Prohres left two battalions of the 31st Brigade encircled; they broke out by about 25 July.
On 19–20 August 2024 Ukraine ordered the mandatory evacuation of families with children from the Pokrovsk community, where 53,000 people still lived, with the front 12 km from the outskirts.
On 27–28 August 2024 Ukraine lost Novohrodivka in 72 hours at a 4:1 firepower disadvantage.
Butusov said of the loss of Novohrodivka in August 2024 that "no decent fortifications were built".
On 5 September 2024 Pokrovsk railway station closed, evacuation trains moved to Pavlohrad, and 26,000 people were left in the city.
By 4 October 2024 the front was about 7 km from Pokrovsk, 80% of its critical infrastructure was destroyed and 13,050 residents remained.
On 10 October 2024 Russia took Mykolaivka, Krasnyi Yar and Krutyi Yar, "the last settlement before Myrnohrad".
Selydove fell on 29–30 October 2024; Russia claimed it on 29 October.
Russia took 196 km² front-wide on 20–27 October 2024, its fastest week of 2024.
Shevchenko fell to Russia on 15 December 2024.
In December 2024 Metinvest suspended the Pishchane shaft, which supplied half its coal.

Ukrainian forces retook Lysivka on 20 February 2025.

In May 2025 Mordvichev left the Center group of forces, and Solodchuk was reported to take over.
Koptieve fell on 1 July 2025.
Russian forces entered Novoekonomichne on 6–7 July 2025.
Razine fell on 13 July 2025.
In July 2025 Russian drones began to achieve air-interdiction effects on the supply roads to Pokrovsk, which ISW says denied Ukraine the use of Pokrovsk as a logistics hub.

In early August 2025 three Russian groups of about 50 walked 14 days from Selydove into Pokrovsk, about 600 m a day, and about 30 of the 150 arrived.

The Pokrovsk map box is about 45 × 45 km, from Kucheriv Yar and Zolotyi Kolodiaz (the tip of the Dobropillia salient) in the north to Selydove and Novohrodivka in the south, and from Udachne in the west to Prohres and Ocheretyne in the east.
Avdiivka, the start line of February 2024, sits 45 km south-east of Pokrovsk, just off the map box.
Pokrovsk stands about 60 km south-west of Kramatorsk.
Pokrovsk stands about 100 km east of Pavlohrad, the rear railhead used for the evacuation.
Pokrovsk is a road and rail hub with a pre-war population of about 60,000.
The railway that cuts east–west through the centre of Pokrovsk became the front line inside the city.
Pokrovsk railway station was reached by a Russian infiltration team in October 2025.
The Dinas microdistrict is in eastern Pokrovsk, on the road to Rodynske and Myrnohrad.
Myrnohrad (Dymytrov) is a mining town 7 km east of Pokrovsk with a pre-war population of about 46,000.
Rivne and Svitle are the two villages between Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad that carried the last road into Myrnohrad in December 2025.
Rodynske is a town 9 km north of Pokrovsk on the T0515 supply road, held by Azov units into January 2026.
Krasnyi Lyman was the north-east jaw of the Russian pincer, 4 km north of Myrnohrad.
Hryshyne is a village 9 km north-west of Pokrovsk and was the next Russian objective in March 2026.
Kotlyne, Pishchane, Shevchenko and Udachne were the scene of the Russian south-west turning move of December 2024 – January 2025, and of the Pokrovske coal mine.
Zvirove and Troianda were on the southern approach to Pokrovsk that the infiltrators used.

text: Pokrovsk sits where several supply highways meet, and its railway station was regionally significant until it closed on 5 September 2024.
In January 2025 Russia cut the T-0504 to Kostiantynivka (the H-32) and the T-0406 to Mezhova.
From July 2025 Russian drones attacked the T-0515 north through Rodynske and Bilytske to Dobropillia, and the T-0514 Dobropillia–Lyman road.
The T-0514 Dobropillia–Lyman road was closed to civilians from 16 July 2025.
The M-30/E-50 to Pavlohrad on the western flank of Pokrovsk was held by the 32nd Brigade.
The same highway runs from Selydove into Pokrovsk from the south, and the November 2025 fog column came in on it.
In December 2025 only roads through Rivne and Svitle remained into Myrnohrad.
The Kazennyi Torets and the Vovcha are the named river lines on the Pokrovsk axis.
Novoekonomichne's reservoirs, river line, industrial zone and two spoil heaps made it "a fortress".
In OSM, 67% of the 100 km² sample box west of Pokrovsk is mapped as farmland.
Fields in the sample box west of Pokrovsk have a median of 65 ha and median dimensions of 625 × 1,348 m.
Shelterbelts west of Pokrovsk run NNW–SSE and are under-mapped in OSM, at only 0.28 km per km².
Tracks in the sample box west of Pokrovsk run at 0.55 km per km², and primary to tertiary roads at 0.13 km per km².
The sample box west of Pokrovsk holds 2,758 buildings in eight settlements.
Villages west of Pokrovsk sit along wooded balkas.
A 1 km treeline near Pokrovsk was the unit of defence: an exposed 80 × 30 m trench in it was destroyed, while two concealed holes held for 10 days.
The August 2025 infiltrators near Dobropillia used ravines running north–south and the summer foliage.
Russian mechanised assaults near Pokrovsk resumed by mid-April 2025 as the ground hardened.
The Dobropillia breach of 7–14 August 2025 came in dry, clear summer weather, 25–30 °C with little rain, and sunrise about 05:20 local.
Foliage and thermal blankets, not fog, hid the August 2025 infiltrators at Dobropillia.
The Russian armoured attacks on Shakhove were timed to rain and morning fog on 6, 9 and 13 October 2025.
On 5–12 November 2025 ERA5 shows overcast, near-saturated air at Pokrovsk, with daily mean relative humidity of 86–96% and light wind.
The research file's fog proxy counts 6–10 hours of fog a day at Pokrovsk on 5–7, 10 and 12 November 2025.

text: In the November 2025 fog more than 300 Russians got into Pokrovsk.
A Russian column of cars and bikes drove into Pokrovsk in fog on 9 November 2025.
Wet weather disadvantaged light FPVs at Pokrovsk.
Up to 10 infiltrators a day got into Pokrovsk on sunny days and 30–40 on rainy ones.
On 1–2 December 2025 Pokrovsk was overcast at 4–6 °C, with 7 mm of rain on 2 December.
The Russian capture claim of 1 December 2025 and the turtle-tank assault of 2 December came in fog.
In December sunset at Pokrovsk is about 16:40, giving about 8.5 hours of daylight.
Pokrovsk fell in deep cold: −15 °C on 17 and 20 January 2026 and −18 °C on 4 February, with a thin snow cover of 3–7 cm.
The 7th Corps said the January 2026 cold caused Russian hypothermia and frostbite losses.
Icing hampers fibre-optic FPVs.
From July 2024 to June 2025 the Russian approach to Pokrovsk was run by the Center Group of Forces under Col. Gen. Andrei Mordvichev until he became Ground Forces commander in May 2025.
Col. Gen. Valery Solodchuk was reported to take over the Center Group of Forces in May 2025.
The 2nd CAA's 27th Motor Rifle Division (506th and 589th regiments) and 15th Motor Rifle Brigade attacked Pokrovsk from the south and south-west in 2024–25.
The 41st CAA's 90th Tank Division (239th Tank Regiment, 228th and 428th regiments) and 35th, 55th and 74th Motor Rifle Brigades took Pishchane and cut the western roads from Pokrovsk in January 2025.
The 1st DNR Corps, from 2025 the 51st CAA, fought on the eastern flank of Pokrovsk at Prohres, Vozdvyzhenka and Myroliubivka with the 1st "Slavic", 5th, 110th and 114th brigades.
The 8th CAA (20th and 150th divisions) and the 68th Corps (39th Brigade) fought along the Kazennyi Torets in spring and summer 2025.
Forbes put Russian strength at Pokrovsk at about 40,000 against about 12,000 Ukrainians in August 2024.
Radio Svoboda put Russian strength on the Pokrovsk axis at 50,000–60,000 in May 2025.
Syrskyi put Russian strength on the Pokrovsk axis at 111,000 in June 2025.
Mashovets put Russian strength on the Pokrovsk axis at 110,000–112,000, with 500–520 tanks, at the end of July 2025.
The Khortytsia operational-strategic group held the Pokrovsk sector in July 2024.
notes: Forbes names the Tavriya group instead

text: Forbes named the Tavriya group as holding the Pokrovsk sector in September 2024.
Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi took command of the Khortytsia group in late January 2025.
Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi led the Donetsk operational-tactical group in April 2025.
In July–August 2024 the 31st, 47th (Abrams) and 110th Mechanised Brigades fought at Prohres.
In September 2024 the 25th Airborne, 59th, 68th Jaeger, 117th and 15th NG "Kara-Dag" brigades held the southern salient and Selydove, reinforced by the 12th Azov and 93rd.
In winter 2024–25 the French-trained 155th "Anne of Kyiv" and the 157th brigades fought at Pokrovsk and were both broken up after failing.
The 425th "Skelia" Assault Regiment and the NG "Chervona Kalyna" fought in the February 2025 counter-attacks at Pokrovsk.
In July 2025 the 17th, 38th Marine and 142nd brigades held the eastern flank of Pokrovsk.
In July 2025 the 32nd Brigade held the western flank of Pokrovsk.
From July 2025 to February 2026 Col. Gen. Valery Solodchuk commanded the Russian Center Group of Forces at Pokrovsk.
Kovalov counted more than 110,000 Russian troops on the Pokrovsk front in August 2025.
Zelensky said there were about 170,000 Russian troops in Donetsk Oblast on 31 October 2025.
Axe gives about 150,000 Russians against about 30,000 Ukrainians at Pokrovsk, a 5:1 ratio.
Zelensky put the force ratio at Pokrovsk at 8:1 in Russia's favour.
The 7th Corps saw 11,000 Russian troops committed to the encirclement of Pokrovsk and 27,000 in its zone, with about 100 tanks, up to 260 AFVs and up to 160 guns and mortars.
About 150,000 Russian troops remained on the Pokrovsk axis in mid-February 2026.

In the south-west of and inside Pokrovsk the 2nd CAA fielded the 27th Motor Rifle Division (439th, 506th, 589th regiments), the 30th and 15th Motor Rifle Brigades, and the mobilised 1435th and 1441st regiments.
North-west of Pokrovsk the 41st CAA fielded the 35th and 74th Motor Rifle Brigades and the 1452nd Regiment, and the 90th Tank Division (6th, 80th, 239th Tank Regiments) also fought there.

North-east of Pokrovsk, at Myrnohrad, Rodynske and Dobropillia, the 51st CAA (the former 1st DNR Corps) fielded the 1st, 5th, 9th, 110th, 114th and 132nd Motor Rifle Brigades, the 56th Spetsnaz Battalion and the 80th Sparta reconnaissance battalion.
8th CAA elements and naval infantry fought on the Dobropillia flank.
From August 2025 Russia reinforced Pokrovsk with naval infantry: the 155th (Pacific), 336th (Baltic) and 40th brigades.
The 76th Guards Air Assault Division arrived at Pokrovsk from the south in December 2025 and was worn out by late January 2026.
Russian drone and special units on the Pokrovsk axis included Rubikon, Sudny Den, Grom-Kaskad ("Irish"), Archangels and the 3rd GRU Spetsnaz Brigade.
ISW judged the 51st and 2nd CAAs "severely degraded" by December 2025.
From July 2025 to February 2026 the 7th Rapid Reaction (Air Assault) Corps under Brig. Gen. Yevhen Lasiychuk ran the defence of Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad.
The "Pokrovsk Tactical Group" held the northern sector in August 2025 and was described as "completely failing to hold the defence" there.

cites.quote: completely failing to hold the defence

text: The Pokrovsk garrison was the 68th Jaeger and 155th Mechanised Brigades, then the 425th Assault Regiment "Skelia" in the north.
The 32nd Mechanised Brigade held the western flank of Pokrovsk on the Pavlohrad highway.
Myrnohrad and its corridor were held by the 25th Airborne, 38th and 35th Marine, and 79th Air Assault Brigades.
The 82nd and 95th Air Assault Brigades fought around Rodynske.
The Dobropillia reserve was the National Guard's 1st Azov Corps under Denys Prokopenko, with its 14th "Chervona Kalyna" and 20th "Liubart" Brigades.

Alongside the 1st Azov Corps at Dobropillia fought the 93rd Mechanised, 4th NG "Rubizh", the "Da Vinci" battalion, the 33rd Mechanised with the 225th Assault Regiment, the 79th and 82nd Air Assault Brigades, and the 132nd Reconnaissance Battalion.
Ukrainian special forces at Pokrovsk included HUR (the Black Hawk landing), the SSO 3rd Regiment (Sword Group), the SBU's Ivan Franko Group, Military Law Enforcement and the National Police.
Ukrainian drone units at Pokrovsk included Magyar's Birds (USF) and the Peaky Blinders drone unit.
Ukrainian sources speak of a "catastrophic shortage of infantry" at Pokrovsk.
An officer told Hromadske that 1,000–1,500 men could be trapped in Myrnohrad without a regrouping order.

observations.subject: Ukrainian troops at risk of encirclement

text: Ukrainian losses in the battle for Pokrovsk are not published.
The contested zone near Pokrovsk was about 1 km deep on 1 January 2025 and five to eight times wider by 2026.
ISW reported in August 2025 that Ukrainian sources put the kill zone at "at least 10 kilometers" from the line, against 0.5–2 km in 2024.
In August 2025 soldiers spoke of a "20-kilometre kill zone" near Dobropillia.
By January 2026 soldiers near Myrnohrad said both sides' kill zones had grown "to about 30 kilometers".
In December 2025 the National Guard put kill zones on the Pokrovsk and Dobropillia axes at up to 30 km deep, with the most intense band 5–10 km.
By July 2026 the 7th Air Assault Corps measured the kill zone on its sector at 20–25 km, with drones causing 70–80% of damage.
From July 2025 Russian drones achieved battlefield air interdiction against the supply roads to Pokrovsk, and ISW judged that this already denied Ukraine the use of Pokrovsk as a logistics hub.
The key roads under Russian drone interdiction were the T-0514 Dobropillia road and the T-0515 through Rodynske.
Serhii Sternenko said in November 2025 that "virtually every vehicle heading into the city comes under attack… The main losses aren't at the positions, but on the road".

cites.quote: Virtually every vehicle heading into the city comes under attack… The main losses aren't at the positions, but on the road

text: Medics said in November 2025 that vehicles could get no closer than 10–15 km to the Pokrovsk front.
Ukrainian troops walked 10–15 km to their positions at Pokrovsk in October 2025.
By the beginning of summer 2025 Russian FPVs, fibre-optic ones included, "controlled all of the entrances to Pokrovsk from the sky".

cites.quote: controlled all of the entrances to Pokrovsk from the sky

text: In late July 2025 Russia hit "two or three Ukrainian vehicles daily" on the T0515 through Rodynske.

cites.quote: two or three Ukrainian vehicles daily

text: By 6 November 2025 less than 5 km of drone-infested fields linked Myrnohrad to the rest of the front.

metric_new.label: Width of a supply corridor or gap between pincers

text: Russian means of road interdiction at Pokrovsk included longer-range FPVs, thermobaric warheads and "waiter" drones parked along roads.
Russian radio and fibre-optic FPVs with thermal cameras made night only slightly safer than day on the Pokrovsk roads.
Russia was said to hold a 10:1 drone advantage at Pokrovsk in October 2025.
Rubikon, the Center for Advanced Unmanned Technologies, was founded on 2 August 2024.
Rubikon had about 1,450 people in March 2025 and about 5,000 by spring 2026.
More than a quarter of Rubikon's strikes hit Ukrainian drone teams.
Rubikon and Sudny Den arrived in this part of Donetsk Oblast "over the spring" of 2025; a 68th Brigade pilot said "in a day they torched eight of our cars".

cites.quote: in a day they torched eight of our cars

observations.subject: Ukrainian cars destroyed in a day

text: Some of the Rubikon crews that had worked against the Kursk salient moved near Pokrovsk.
After cutting off Sudzha in February–March 2025, Rubikon was moved to the Pokrovsk direction to interdict logistics and kill drone operators.
A 7th Corps spokesman confirmed Rubikon's presence at Pokrovsk: "Their tactic is to cut off the Ukrainian Defense Forces' logistical routes".

cites.quote: Their tactic is to cut off the Ukrainian Defense Forces' logistical routes

text: Ukrainian soldiers said Pokrovsk was "like a holiday" before Rubikon arrived.
Rubikon FPV teams held the single road into Myrnohrad "almost constantly under… fire control".
Other named Russian drone units on the Pokrovsk axis were Sudny Den (Judgment Day), the "Irish" (Grom-Kaskad) and Archangels.
HUR struck a claimed Rubikon base near Avdiivka in early November 2025 with long-range FPVs.
In January 2026 Starlink-equipped Rubikon drones reaching the E-50 behind Pokrovsk triggered the Starlink whitelist.

In July 2025 three Russian groups of about 50 walked 14 days from Selydove to Pokrovsk, about 600 m a day, supplied by drone drops and wearing cloaks; about 30 of 150 arrived and the rest were killed by drone drops.
notes: the timeline dates this walk to early August 2025

text: The August 2025 Russian Dobropillia force of 200–300 men had also walked about two weeks from Selydove.
Russian infiltrators at Pokrovsk moved in groups of three "with the expectation that two will be destroyed", up to 300 men a day.

cites.quote: with the expectation that two will be destroyed

text: About 100 Russian infiltration groups a day moved on Pokrovsk in November 2025.
By January 2026 Russians infiltrated as single men.
Up to 10 Russian infiltrators got in on a sunny day and 30–40 on a rainy one.
Russian infiltrators targeted Ukrainian drone crews first, engaging them at close range so that they could not launch.
Russian infiltrators carried two radios, one to pass the line and one to correct fire from a "burrow".
Some Russian infiltrators at Pokrovsk wore civilian clothes.
Mashovets describes three phases of Russian infiltration: preparation (Spetsnaz find supply roads and drone sites), execution, then exploitation by many small groups.
On 9 November 2025, in fog, a Russian column of cars and motorbikes drove into southern Pokrovsk on the Selydove highway.
Russian motorcycle groups of 6–8 bikes carried 2–3 EW sets, and few groups survived.
In March 2026 quad bikes carrying up to four men replaced motorcycles for Russian flanking runs near Myrnohrad.
Russian company to reinforced-battalion columns attacked Shakhove on 6, 9, 13, 16 and 27 October 2025, timed to rain and fog.
Turtle tanks of the 40th Naval Infantry Brigade attacked near Razine on 2 December 2025 and lost 11 vehicles.
ISW predicted that infiltration alone could not generate enough mass to clear Pokrovsk, forcing Russia to bring troops in by vehicle in bad weather.
Russia dropped 850 KABs on Pokrovsk in October 2025, and 156 in one autumn day.
Some Ukrainian brigades moved most forward supply to UGVs and heavy Vampire multicopters; one Air Assault brigade flew 10–12 t a month, about 80% of its deliveries.

observations.subject: one Air Assault brigade, per month
share of the brigade's deliveries by drone and UGV

text: From the first weeks of the city fight in October 2025 no Ukrainian vehicle could get through the corridor to Myrnohrad, so every supply run was made by drone or UGV, and the UGVs "usually don't survive the trip".
Large Ukrainian bomber drones supplying Myrnohrad could still lift 60 mm mortar bombs but not 120 mm ones, and keeping drone teams in fuel took many sorties.

observations.subject: mortar bombs that bomber drones could lift
mortar bombs too heavy for bomber drones

text: In January 2026 the defenders of Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad were supplied by "heavy drones and ground robotic complexes".

cites.quote: heavy drones and ground robotic complexes

text: NATO said Myrnohrad was being resupplied by drone in December 2025.
The 93rd Brigade used gun-armed UGVs in the Dobropillia counter-attack.
UGVs cannot cross rivers and stick in mud and craters.
On 15 October 2025 a Zmiy UGV carried a wounded man out under 152 mm fire, a mine blast and an FPV hit, after losing its link for 1.5 hours.
The Zmiy UGV has a 500 kg payload, a speed of 10 km/h and a 20 km range.
SSO's Sword Group cleared a blocking position so that a ground robot could evacuate three wounded.
A 25th Brigade UGV took a direct FPV hit and still brought out two wounded in a six-hour mission.
Near Pokrovsk in July 2025 the wounded had to "wait days" for evacuation.
By November 2025 some seriously wounded Ukrainians near Pokrovsk lay in position for two weeks, and Red Cross-marked UGVs drew fire.
In 2025 UGVs typically brought wounded out from 2–5 km at night to medical posts 7 km or more behind the line.
By late October 2025 medics said evacuation of the wounded from Pokrovsk was nearly impossible because all the bridges had been blown.
On the drive into Pokrovsk in June 2025 anti-drone nets were "helpful, but enemy drones simply need to find the entrance or create one", and one net hung down across the road.

cites.quote: helpful, but enemy drones simply need to find the entrance or create one

text: Syrskyi ordered "anti-drone tunnels" and barriers against "total infiltration" on 2 August 2025.
By October 2025 Russian FPVs "cut through anti-drone netting" on the Myrnohrad route.
Russia had netted its own roads since February 2025.
Fog hurts the side that relies on drones and helps the side moving on the ground.
Fog let more than 300 Russians into Pokrovsk on 7–12 November 2025.
Fog was the only cover under which Ukrainian vehicles could reach Myrnohrad and under which Ukrainians could leave Pokrovsk, as a Russian milblogger admitted.
Ukrainian counters to Russian movement in fog were UGVs as ground spotters, SIGINT direction-finding and AI-assisted FPVs.
Joint teams of SSO, HUR, SBU, Military Law Enforcement and police hunted Russian infiltrators in Pokrovsk building by building.
Radio intercepts gave away Russian call signs, and in one Myrnohrad clearance Ukrainian troops called out in Russian, "Kedr, we're your own", and walked in.
Ukrainian loudspeaker drones broadcast surrender instructions to Russian infiltrators.

Russian flags appeared on the western entrance sign of Pokrovsk on 29 October 2025 (destroyed within an hour), on a ruined mine in Myrnohrad on 14 November, and in the Pokrovsk centre in the Russian MoD video of 1 December.
ISW treated the December 2025 Russian flags in Myrnohrad as infiltration missions that "did not change control of terrain".

cites.quote: did not change control of terrain

text: Ukraine answered the Russian flag raids with a flag on a live drone feed in northern Pokrovsk on 9 December 2025.
In July 2025 three Russian groups of about 50 men moved from Selydove to the Pishchane industrial zone, then crept about 600 m a day towards Zakhysnykiv Ukrainy Street in Pokrovsk.
On the July 2025 walk to Pokrovsk drones dropped the Russian infiltrators' water and food, and cloaks hid them from thermal cameras; about 120 died from drone drops and some 30 reached the city.

On 21 July 2025 DeepState reported that Russians walked into Pokrovsk through Zvirove because one brigade had no infantry left and positions were misreported, and the 155th and 68th brigades had to plug the hole.
On 11–17 August 2025 a 15 km wedge, the Dobropillia "rabbit ears", appeared on the map in five days.

observations.subject: time for the wedge to form

text: DeepState and the General Staff publicly disagreed about the Dobropillia breach in August 2025.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: In August 2025 the Azov Corps arrived at Dobropillia, and the 93rd Brigade's tanks and gun robots cleared Zolotyi Kolodiaz, Hruzke and Vesele.
On 22 October 2025 the 132nd Reconnaissance Battalion retook Kucheriv Yar and captured more than 50 Russians, and civilians were found in basements.
At about 20 October 2025 a Russian infiltration team reached the centre of Pokrovsk, killed civilians and was destroyed inside a station building.
On 29 October 2025, from 09:40 to 10:40, a Russian flag went up on the western entrance sign of Pokrovsk by the Pavlohrad highway and was destroyed within an hour.
In late October 2025 HUR special forces landed by helicopter in the northern part of Pokrovsk, in an operation overseen by Budanov, to hold the corridor out.
Russia claimed all 11 HUR special forces of the late-October 2025 landing were killed, and Ukraine denied it.
On 9 November 2025 Russian infantry on civilian cars and motorbikes drove up the Selydove highway into southern Pokrovsk under fog, and 68th Brigade drones partly destroyed the column.

From November 2025 to January 2026 Myrnohrad was reached by a single road with 1–3 km of corridor and Rubikon FPVs overhead; vehicles could run only on the foggiest days, and a stretch of clear weather could doom the garrison.

metric_new.label: Width of a supply corridor or gap between pincers

text: On 2 December 2025 a Russian naval-infantry column near Razine hit an anti-tank ditch in fog, and 11 vehicles burned.
On 9 December 2025, eight days after Moscow's claim, Skala soldiers waved a Ukrainian flag in northern Pokrovsk for the BBC.
The Zmiy UGV evacuated a wounded soldier under 152 mm fire, and gun robots fought in residential yards.
On 28 January 2026 Russian command posts and a commandant's office moved into Myrnohrad; Ukrainian marines in the north were told to "not let them out of the city", and there was no order to leave.

cites.quote: not let them out of the city

text: According to the American analyst Andrew Perpetua, Ukrainian commanders in summer 2025 deliberately left some trenches north-east of Pokrovsk empty so that brigades could refit: "Sacrifice ground for time while refitting and then you can attack later".

cites.quote: Sacrifice ground for time while refitting and then you can attack later

text: The Dobropillia breach of August 2025 came through the gaps left by empty trenches north-east of Pokrovsk.
The Kyiv Independent places the weak point of the Dobropillia breach at the seam between two exhausted National Guard brigades and blames false reporting up the chain.
In August 2025 Syrskyi sent the last large reserve, the 1st Azov Corps, against the Dobropillia salient rather than to Pokrovsk.
After the 1st Azov Corps was committed, the Dobropillia salient was gone by late October 2025.
David Axe, citing the analyst "Delwin", argues that the Dobropillia salient was a "counter-fixation axis" that kept Azov out of Pokrovsk itself.
CIT judged Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad "effectively lost" because the reserves went to Dobropillia.
Farrell calls the Dobropillia operation costly "fire-fighting" rather than a successful counter-offensive.
Black Bird Group said Ukraine should have withdrawn from Pokrovsk by about mid-summer 2025.
On 4 November 2025 CIT said "It is time… to abandon Myrnohrad and the area south of it".

cites.quote: It is time… to abandon Myrnohrad and the area south of it

text: Clément Molin wrote that observers "struggle to understand Syrskyi's strategy" at Pokrovsk.
Sternenko pointed to a pattern of late Ukrainian withdrawals at Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Sudzha.
Syrskyi's line was that there was "no encirclement or blockade": "Pokrovsk – we hold. Myrnohrad – we hold".

cites.quote: Pokrovsk – we hold. Myrnohrad – we hold

text: Soldiers told CNN on 8 November 2025 and Ukrainska Pravda on 28 January 2026 that there was no order to withdraw from Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad.
The 68th and 155th brigades began leaving Pokrovsk on foot from about 27 October 2025.
On 8 December 2025 Ukraine made an "organized maneuver" out of the salient south of Pokrovsk.
By February 2026 Ukraine had fallen back a short distance north of Pokrovsk; no official order to withdraw from either town was found.
In late October 2025 Syrskyi ordered SSO, HUR, SBU and military-police groups into Pokrovsk rather than a brigade.
DeepState called for a mop-up of Pokrovsk "by a full brigade, not by small special-forces groups".

cites.quote: by a full brigade, not by small special-forces groups

text: DeepState's public depiction of the Dobropillia breach prompted faster reaction from higher command than official channels, according to a battalion commander.
The Dnipro group's spokesman told viewers not to believe unofficial maps of the Dobropillia breach.
After the Starlink cut-off in January–February 2026, Kyiv moved units including the 425th Assault Regiment south to counter-attack at Huliaipole, accepting the loss of ground north of Pokrovsk.
Axe judged moving units from Pokrovsk to Huliaipole "a hard decision, but one that has paid off".

cites.quote: a hard decision, but one that has paid off

text: ISW judged that Russia was trying to encircle and storm Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad at the same time.
In November 2025 Russia seemed to shift to closing the ring around Pokrovsk from the west, while fixing Ukrainian troops inside to prevent an orderly withdrawal.
Russian armour at Pokrovsk was held back until infantry had accumulated, then committed in fog.
Gerasimov said on 26 October 2025 that up to 10,000 Ukrainians were encircled at Pokrovsk, which pro-war bloggers and ISW disputed.
Gerasimov reported the capture of "Krasnoarmeysk" (Pokrovsk) to Putin on 30 November 2025.
Peskov announced the capture of Pokrovsk on 1 December 2025, just before the Witkoff talks.
Putin called Pokrovsk a "good base" for advancing in "any direction".
Solodchuk claimed Myrnohrad and Rodynske on 27 December 2025.
Ukrainian officers say Russia used Pokrovsk as leverage in the US-led talks rather than for its own value.
Russian officials credited the capture of Pokrovsk to the 27th Motor Rifle Division (2nd CAA) with the 506th and 1435th regiments and the 30th Brigade.
Russian officials credited the capture of Myrnohrad to the 5th Brigade (51st CAA) and the 1435th Regiment, and of Rodynske to the 9th Brigade.
Russian milbloggers admitted that no encirclement of Pokrovsk existed in October 2025.
A Russian milblogger admitted that fog let Ukrainians exit Pokrovsk.
A Russian milblogger admitted that the base of the Dobropillia penetration was too narrow for logistics.
A Russian brigade commander described about 3 km of advance towards Myrnohrad in four months.

observations.subject: advance towards Myrnohrad in four months

text: A Ukrainian officer said in February 2026 that Russia "officially announced the capture of Myrnohrad last week — and then quietly removed the report".

cites.quote: officially announced the capture of Myrnohrad last week — and then quietly removed the report

text: Russia still uses the pre-2016 names Krasnoarmeysk for Pokrovsk and Dimitrov for Myrnohrad.

ISW concluded that the fall of Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad did not open the way north: Russia had not exploited Pokrovsk as of late February 2026, Hryshyne 2 km north-west still held, and the Fortress Belt was untouched.
ISW assessed the 51st and 2nd CAAs as "severely degraded".

effect: denied Pokrovsk as a logistics hub; vehicles held 10–15 km back
rationale: Russian FPVs, including Rubikon's, put every road into Pokrovsk under fire control and hit vehicles daily, so the main losses were on the road and vehicles could get no closer than 10–15 km.

measure: Ukrainian supply routes and drone operators on the Pokrovsk axis
effect: road lethality rose sharply; Myrnohrad road held under near-constant fire control
rationale: Rubikon was moved to Pokrovsk after Sudzha to interdict logistics and kill drone operators; more than a quarter of its strikes hit drone teams, and it held the single road into Myrnohrad under fire control.

effect: kept garrisons supplied, but UGVs usually did not survive the trip
rationale: When no vehicle could reach Myrnohrad, every supply run went by drone or UGV, and some brigades moved most forward supply (about 80% in one) to UGVs and Vampires.
Large bomber drones lifted supplies into Myrnohrad when roads were closed, but could carry 60 mm mortar bombs and not 120 mm ones, and fuel took many sorties.
UGVs on the Myrnohrad run usually did not survive the trip; Red Cross-marked UGVs drew fire and a 25th Brigade UGV took a direct FPV hit.
UGVs cannot cross rivers and stick in mud and craters.
Nets on the drive into Pokrovsk were helpful against FPVs, though drones could find or make an entrance.
By October 2025 Russian FPVs cut through the anti-drone netting on the Myrnohrad route, and drones could find or create entrances.

effect: Russian infiltrators accumulated inside Pokrovsk and opened the Dobropillia wedge
rationale: Russian infantry seeped past thinly held and empty positions in groups of two or three, walked in via Zvirove where a brigade had run out of infantry, and opened the 15 km Dobropillia wedge past empty trenches.

effect: about 80% of one infiltration wave killed
rationale: Ukrainian drone drops killed about 120 of 150 infiltrators on the July 2025 walk from Selydove.
Cloaks hid the July 2025 infiltrators from Ukrainian thermal cameras.

counter: killing drone crews at close range
rationale: Infiltrators went for Ukrainian drone crews first, engaging at close range so they could not launch, and Rubikon struck drone teams.
Joint SSO, HUR, SBU, military-police and police teams hunted infiltrators building by building in Pokrovsk, and radio intercepts and deception helped clear Myrnohrad positions.
Loudspeaker drones broadcast surrender instructions to infiltrators.
Fog hurts the side relying on drones: in the November 2025 fog more than 300 Russians got into Pokrovsk and a vehicle column drove in.

effect: vehicle runs possible only on the foggiest days
rationale: Fog was the only cover under which Ukrainian vehicles could reach Myrnohrad and Ukrainians could leave Pokrovsk.

counter: UGV ground spotters, SIGINT direction-finding and AI-assisted FPVs
rationale: Ukraine countered Russian movement in fog with UGV spotters, SIGINT direction-finding and AI-assisted FPVs.
A Russian naval-infantry turtle-tank column in fog near Razine hit an anti-tank ditch and lost 11 vehicles.

counter: HUR long-range FPV strikes on drone bases
rationale: HUR struck a claimed Rubikon base near Avdiivka with long-range FPVs.
Starlink-equipped Rubikon drones reaching the E-50 behind Pokrovsk triggered the Starlink whitelist, which grounded Russian drones that used it.
The 93rd Brigade's tanks and gun robots cleared infiltrators from Zolotyi Kolodiaz, Hruzke and Vesele in the Dobropillia counter-attack.
Radio and fibre-optic FPVs with thermal cameras made night only slightly safer than day on the roads.
DeepState's public depiction of the Dobropillia breach prompted faster reaction from higher command than official channels.
Russian motorcycle groups carried 2–3 EW sets per 6–8 bikes, yet few groups survived.
